chronic_conditions: History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) with t(15;17)

filing.block_desc: Benign neoplasms, except benign neuroendocrine tumors (D10-D36)

encounters.cc: Persistent milky nipple discharge and irregular menstrual periods over the past 8 months

lines: Persistent milky nipple discharge and irregular menstrual periods over the past 8 months
The discharge has been present for about 8 months and is milky in appearance, non-bloody, and occurs spontaneously.
Her menses occur every 6 to 8 weeks and are lighter than they used to be.
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) with t(15;17)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) PRN every 4-6 hours
She has never been pregnant and does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use recreational drugs.
She denies recent weight changes, headaches, or visual symptoms.
On physical exam, gentle pressure on both breasts elicits milky discharge from the nipples.
There are no masses, skin changes, or signs of inflammation.
A serum pregnancy test is negative. Laboratory testing reveals elevated serum prolactin.
MRI of the brain shows a 6-mm lesion in the anterior pituitary.

encounters.cc: Unintentional weight loss, heat intolerance, and frequent palpitations over the past 3 months

lines: Unintentional weight loss, heat intolerance, and frequent palpitations over the past 3 months
She returns six months after her evaluation for galactorrhea, with unintentional weight loss, heat intolerance, and frequent palpitations over the past 3 months and menses irregular for 6 months.
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) with t(15;17)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) PRN every 4-6 hours
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
Physical examination shows a diffusely enlarged, non-tender thyroid gland and a fine resting tremor in her hands.
On further examination, she has mild bilateral lid lag and periorbital swelling.

encounters.cc: Several months of restlessness, irritability, and insomnia with self-directed thyroid hormone use

lines: Several months of restlessness, irritability, and insomnia with self-directed thyroid hormone use
The patient with a plurihormonal pituitary macroadenoma and history of Graves disease returns for follow-up.
She has unintentionally lost 10 pounds over the past 3 months despite having a good appetite.
Her sister reports that the patient has become obsessed with her appearance and takes triiodothyronine she purchased online.
The patient denies chest pain, tremors, or recent illness.
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) with t(15;17)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) PRN every 4-6 hours
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
Physical exam reveals a heart rate of 106/min and blood pressure of 132/76 mm Hg.
She appears anxious but is alert and cooperative.
The thyroid gland is non-palpable with no tenderness or enlargement.
There is no lid lag, proptosis, or pretibial edema.
Laboratory studies and a radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) scan are ordered.

encounters.cc: Persistent fatigue, anxiety, and difficulty sleeping during pregnancy with weight loss despite increased appetite

lines: Persistent fatigue, anxiety, and difficulty sleeping during pregnancy with weight loss despite increased appetite
The patient returns for obstetric care with a history of plurihormonal pituitary macroadenoma and Graves disease, previously managed by Endocrinology.
She reports feeling her heart racing frequently, experiencing excessive sweating, and having frequent loose stools.
Despite eating more than usual, she has lost 5 kg over this period.
Her pregnancy has otherwise been uncomplicated.
She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or visual changes.
- Secondary hyperthyroidism due to TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) with t(15;17)
She is taking prenatal vitamins regularly.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) PRN every 4-6 hours
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On examination, her pulse is 116/min, blood pressure is 122/76 mmHg, and BMI is 18 kg/m².
Her skin is warm and moist, and a fine tremor is noted in both hands.
Thyroid examination reveals a diffusely enlarged, non-tender gland without nodules.
Fetal heart tones are normal, and there is no lower extremity edema.
She is started on appropriate pharmacologic therapy for her condition.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain on postoperative day 2 following Cesarean section

lines: Sudden-onset shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain on postoperative day 2 following Cesarean section

The patient is a 30-year-old female with a plurihormonal pituitary macroadenoma and Graves disease, with hyperthyroidism in pregnancy, and presents on postoperative day 2 following uncomplicated Cesarean section.
She develops sudden-onset shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain upon standing to void.
- Secondary hyperthyroidism due to TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) with t(15;17)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) PRN every 4-6 hours
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
Arterial blood gas analysis shows pH 7.48, pCO 2 30 mm Hg, and pO 2 70 mm Hg on room air
A ventilation-perfusion scan and spiral CT of the chest confirm the diagnosis

encounters.cc: Persistent oozing of blood from IV line and central venous catheter insertion sites during admission

lines: Persistent oozing of blood from IV line and central venous catheter insertion sites during admission
This patient with acute promyelocytic leukemia and recent postpartum PE presents with bleeding.
During her current admission, the nurses note repeated blood-staining of her dressings and slow, continuous bleeding from venipuncture sites.
She denies any trauma or recent surgeries.
- Secondary hyperthyroidism due to TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) with t(15;17)
She was recently hospitalized and underwent induction chemotherapy for acute leukemia.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) PRN every 4-6 hours
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On examination, she is alert but appears pale.
Petechiae are noted on her lower extremities, and there is mild bruising on her arms.
She has no active external hemorrhage, but blood continues to ooze from her central line.
A peripheral blood smear is sent and is pending. Basic coagulation studies are ordered.

encounters.cc: Painful oral ulcers and worsening rash with eye redness and pain over the past 3 days

lines: Painful oral ulcers and worsening rash with eye redness and pain over the past 3 days
This 31-year-old with epilepsy, plurihormonal pituitary macroadenoma, Graves disease, and APL with recent DIC presents for evaluation.
She reports that the rash began on her trunk and has spread to her face and extremities, with some areas developing blisters that have ruptured.
She also complains of eye redness and pain.
- Secondary hyperthyroidism due to TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) with t(15;17)
She has a history of epilepsy, well-controlled.
She takes on phenytoin for the past two years.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) PRN every 4-6 hours
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
Her temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, and respiratory rate is 22/min.
Physical examination reveals erythematous macules and atypical targetoid lesions with central dusky purpura and blistering on her trunk, face, and extremities.
Mucosal involvement is noted with hemorrhagic crusting of the lips, oral mucosal erosions, and conjunctival injection.

encounters.cc: Shortness of breath and wheezing for 2 hours after pollen exposure with poor response to rescue inhaler

lines: Shortness of breath and wheezing for 2 hours after pollen exposure with poor response to rescue inhaler

This 32-year-old female with asthma, epilepsy, plurihormonal pituitary macroadenoma, Graves disease, and acute promyelocytic leukemia in remission presents to the emergency department with a 2-hour history of shortness of breath and wheezing.
She reports that her symptoms began after exposure to pollen during a morning walk.
She used her albuterol inhaler twice without significant relief.
- Secondary hyperthyroidism due to TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) with t(15;17)
She has a past medical history of asthma.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) PRN every 4-6 hours
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
She denies fever, chills, or recent illness
Her oxygen saturation is 92% on room air.
Her temperature is 37.1°C, blood pressure is 130/75 mmHg, and pulse is 110 beats per minute.
On examination, she is anxious, tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute, and using accessory muscles to breathe.
Auscultation of the chest reveals diffuse expiratory wheezes.
Arterial blood gas shows a pH of 7.45, PaCO2 of 32 mmHg, PaO2 of 75 mmHg, and HCO3- of 24 mEq/L.
